g1.label: 1. apartment
g1.why: In British English, an apartment is called a ‘flat’.

g2.label: 2. elevator
g2.why: In British English, an elevator is called a ‘lift’.

g3.label: 3. sidewalk
g3.why: In British English, a sidewalk is called the ‘pavement’.

g4.label: 4. cookie
g4.why: In British English, a cookie is called a ‘biscuit’.

g5.label: 5. trunk (of a car)
g5.why: In British English, the trunk of a car is called the ‘boot’.

g6.label: 6. french fries
g6.why: In British English, french fries are called ‘chips’.

g7.label: 7. gas (fuel)
g7.why: In British English, gas (fuel) is called ‘petrol’.

g8.label: 8. vacation
g8.why: In British English, a vacation is called a ‘holiday’.

g9.label: 9. candy
g9.why: In British English, candy is called ‘sweets’.

g10.label: 10. cell phone
g10.why: In British English, a cell phone is called a ‘mobile phone’.

g1.label: 1. The ___ of the house was lovely
g1.why: British English keeps the ‘-our’ ending: colour (American: color).

g2.label: 2. The city ___
g2.why: British English uses ‘-re’ at the end: centre (American: center).

g3.label: 3. ___ my room
g3.why: British English commonly uses ‘-ise’ endings: organise (American: organize).

g4.label: 4. My favourite ___
g4.why: British English keeps the ‘-our’ ending: neighbour (American: neighbor).

g5.label: 5. The ___ was exciting
g5.why: British English uses ‘programme’ for a TV or radio show (American: program).

g6.label: 6. I didn't ___ how late it was
g6.why: British English commonly uses ‘-ise’ endings: realise (American: realize).

g7.label: 7. She had to ___ for being late
g7.why: British English commonly uses ‘-ise’ endings: apologise (American: apologize).

g8.label: 8. The ___ of chocolate
g8.why: British English keeps the ‘-our’ ending: flavour (American: flavor).

g1.label: 1. Americans call a ___
g1.why: The text compares the American word ‘sidewalk’ with the British ‘pavement’.

g2.label: 2. An American goes on ___
g2.why: The text compares an American ‘vacation’ with the British ‘holiday’.

g3.label: 3. The British write ___
g3.why: British spelling keeps the ‘-our’ ending: colour, while Americans write ‘color’.

g4.label: 4. Americans spell it ___
g4.why: American spelling drops the ‘-re’ ending and uses ‘-er’: center.

g5.label: 5. Formal writing avoids ___
g5.why: ‘Don’t’ and ‘can’t’ are contractions, which should be avoided in formal writing.

g6.label: 6. Informal language often uses ___
g6.why: ‘Find out’ is a phrasal verb, common in informal English instead of formal words like ‘discover’.
